⚡ Key Findings for BWSSB & BAF Action
🚨

Nearly half of all consumption has zero wastewater treatment

689 connections (15.8%) have no STP — yet they consume 134 crore litres every month, accounting for 46.6% of total apartment water consumption in this dataset. Every litre consumed becomes untreated effluent.

🏗

Builders are holding 770 Cauvery connections that belong to residents

17.6% of all connections remain in developer or company names — consuming 68 crore L/month. With no RWA in control, there is no resident body to enforce STP compliance, pay bills responsibly, or participate in conservation campaigns.

👤

48.8% of connections are in individual names — a governance grey zone

2,133 buildings with 20+ flats each have their BWSSB connection in a single person's name. These are likely original landowners or plot holders who never formed an RWA. BWSSB has no resident body to engage for conservation or compliance.

🗺

Three zones account for a disproportionate share of consumption

SDID zones E31, S11, and S21 are the top consumers — E31 alone accounts for 40 crore L/month. Zonal campaigns targeting these subdivisions will have the highest conservation impact per effort.

🔵

BAF has 395 member apartments to engage directly

Of 1,307 BAF members, 395 appear in BWSSB's high-consumer list. These are the most accessible targets for BAF's conservation campaign — existing relationships, known contacts, and MC governance structures already in place.

Data source: BWSSB High Water Consumer List, August 2026 · Analysis by Bengaluru Apartments Federation (BAF) · Map built using Google Maps API · 3,627 of 4,375 connections plotted (746 removed as bad geocodes — SDID zone outliers) · BAF membership matched using fuzzy name matching (threshold: 90%) · This document is for internal BAF and BWSSB use only.
